source_reports.citation: Messinger, T., Duda, J.M., Wagner, D.M., O'Shea, P.S., Scott, J.D., and Kandel, C., 2026, Estimation of magnitude and frequency of floods for rural, unregulated streams in and near Virginia and West Virginia: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2025-5110.

notes: Messinger and others, SIR 2025-5110: drainage-area equations for 12 regions across Virginia and West Virginia at 8 AEPs; this file holds the 11 NSS serves for this state, and West Virginia's file holds its own with the same equations. Constants and coefficients from Table 7; AVP, model error variance and SEP from Table 8; site counts and drainage-area ranges from Table 6, which rounds them where NSS keeps more digits. The report prints no covariance, so intervals use the AVP. The report limits the equations to rural, unregulated basins: under 30 percent developed (compare other methods at 10-30 percent) and with a regulation index RI under 0.0040. Those limits are not stored as ranges, because the equations do not use them and flowfreq does not fetch RI.
